notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 13137 (64 FR 50733, Sept. 15, 1999): a pure amending order that rewrites sec. 3 of EO 12975, adds a new sec. 4 (membership/terms) and renumbers and amends sec. 8(b) (termination date moved from Oct. 3, 1999 to Oct. 3, 2001). Its operative effect exists only as amendments to the National Bioethics Advisory Commission order EO 12975. I also read the complete held EO 13316 (68 FR 55255, Sept. 17, 2003). Its Sec. 3(b) revokes, in a list of orders 'which established committees that have terminated or whose work is completed', 'Executive Order 12975, as amended by Executive Orders 13018, 13046, and 13137, establishing the National Bioethics Advisory Commission', expressly naming EO 13137 as part of the revoked instrument; Sec. 6 makes the order effective Sept. 30, 2003. Revoking the amended base order as amended by 13137 removes the only text 13137 amended, so no operative content of 13137 remains in force; nothing in EO 13316 saves any part of 13137 and the original 13137 has no independent continuing command, so no savings clause or partial scope applies. The only history observation (API catalog note 'Amends: EO 12975 / See: EO 13316') and its cross-reference candidate event agree with the held acting text but are editorial leads, not the basis. Earlier endings: EO 13137 sec. 3(c) moved the Commission's own termination to Oct. 3, 2001, so the Commission may have lapsed before 13316 (EO 12975 text not examined here); that would only move the end earlier and cannot make the order current at 2026-10-14. I do not assert the first-end date, which stays a lifecycle gap, nor any status through intervening periods. This is a provisional NO hypothesis only.
